name: Mineral Point
headline: TWG Development built Mineral Point, 34 studio, one- and two-bedroom apartments for households at 30% to 60% AMI in three two-story buildings at 601-607 Butte Avenue on Town of Crested Butte land, with a 2023 Round One 9% credit award; the buildings received temporary certificates of occupancy in summer 2026 but lease-up was still waiting on a management handoff in September 2026.
why_it_matters: It shows a mountain town supplying a remediated former dump site on a 75-year ground lease plus several million dollars of loans and fees to land a 9% deal, and how contractor problems and a management-agreement standoff can push a credit-funded building close to its placed-in-service deadline (one occupied unit per building by 2026-12-31).

status.label: Built (temporary certificates of occupancy, summer 2026); lease-up start not confirmed
status.detail: The Crested Butte News reported on 2026-09-02 that the units were completed and received a temporary certificate of occupancy in early August 2026, but Gunnison County Housing Authority was not yet accepting rental applications because its property management agreement with TWG was still pending (set for its board on 2026-09-15). ColoradoBiz reported on 2026-09-29 that Mineral Point 'has opened', while the property's leasing website still said 'Opening soon' on 2026-10-21. No public record confirms move-ins.

next_step: Watch Gunnison County Housing Authority board actions on the TWG management agreement and Crested Butte News reports of first move-ins before the 2026-12-31 occupancy deadline.

key_numbers.meaning: All at 30% to 60% AMI (4 at 30%, 3 at 40%, 6 at 50%, 21 at 60%); no project-based vouchers.
About $12.5M over 10 years (inferred); the town expected it to raise about $11M of equity. Same amount as requested.
Reported figures moved between $16.6M (2023 estimate), just under $16.9M (2024) and $16.2M (2025), roughly $480,000 to $500,000 per unit (inferred).
Includes site cleanup, predevelopment and a $500,000 gap loan; the application estimated the town's total contribution at over $7.4M ($220,000 per unit).

facts.value: 601, 603, 605, 607 Butte Avenue, Crested Butte, CO 81224 (Sixth Street and Butte Avenue; ColoradoBiz gives 603 Butte Ave.)

background.text: The town declared a housing emergency on 2021-06-07, then ran a master planning process for the Sixth and Butte parcels and chose TWG through a request for proposals; the town also agreed to share predevelopment costs so the project would be permit-ready by May 2023.

The site was part of a historic town dump. The town completed a $2.6M cleanup in fall 2022 under CDPHE's Voluntary Cleanup Program; the buildings have methane and radon vapor mitigation systems, and the town operates the soil gas mitigation system.

The Board of Zoning and Architectural Review approved the design unanimously on 2022-12-20; the design follows the town's National Historic District guidelines, the 2021 building code and the town's all-electric and ZERH requirements.

The application said the town ground lease and the housing authority's role would keep the homes at 30% to 60% AMI in perpetuity, and requested a waiver of the 1.30 debt coverage threshold because net operating income declines over time.

Market study (Novogradac) figures in the application: 5.5% capture rate, about four months to lease up, rents 11% to 59% below market comparables, and rental vacancy below 1% for seven years; Anthracite Place (2014 award) was the only other LIHTC property in town. By September 2026, 67 households were on the interest list.

Construction was late from the start: a delayed state review of right-of-way fire suppression lines held back summer 2024 work, and the town red-tagged the site at least twice; the second stop order (2025-05-29, over debris, OSHA safety, materials storage and no on-site supervisor) was lifted on 2025-06-10.

Move-in targets slipped from fall 2024 (2023 plan) to August 2025, then to February or March 2026, then to summer 2026. In July 2026 the town pulled building A's temporary certificate of occupancy over concrete grade corrections at unit entrances; temporary certificates were in place by early August 2026.

Sizeable equity installments are tied to certificates of occupancy, and TWG must have at least one unit occupied in each building by 2026-12-31 under the credit schedule, according to the town's housing director.
Sixteen middle-income units on the adjacent parcel (planned with High Mountain Concepts, with no income caps but a local-work requirement) are a separate project and not part of the tax credit deal.

discrepancies.text: Reported total cost moved between an estimated $16.6 million in May 2023, $16 million in December 2023, just under $16.9 million in July 2024 and $16.2 million in July 2025.
The application describes a 1.26-acre site, while a 2025 news report describes the leased site as one acre.

ColoradoBiz reported on 2026-09-29 that Mineral Point has opened, but the Crested Butte News reported on 2026-09-02 that the housing authority could not yet accept rental applications, and the property website still showed 'Opening soon' in October 2026.
The application said TWG Construction usually serves as general contractor on TWG projects, while news reports say TWG subcontracted most of the work to Streamline General Contractors.

open_questions: Whether the Gunnison County Housing Authority management agreement was approved on 2026-09-15 and when the first residents moved in; whether the one-unit-per-building occupancy test is met by 2026-12-31.
